q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution

NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release would typically occur in late August 2026 (based on historical patterns where NVIDIA reports quarterly earnings ~4-6 weeks after quarter-end). Today is 2026-08-24, so we are likely **within days to a few weeks** of the actual earnings announcement and forward guidance release. This is an imminent event.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 has already been publicly issued on May 20, 2026 at **$91.0 billion ±2%**, which translates to a range of **$89.2 billion to $92.8 billion**.

The research indicates:
- Wall Street consensus is ~$91.9 billion (comfortably within guidance)
- Q1 FY2027 actual came in at $81.6 billion, beating guidance by ~$2 billion
- The guided range of $89.2B-$92.8B is quite wide (±2%), which NVIDIA uses as standard practice
- A similar outperformance pattern to Q1 could push realized revenue near $95 billion, but that would be **actual results**, not the forward guidance being issued now

The question asks specifically for "forward guidance" that will be "issued in Q2 FY2027 earnings release." Since guidance was already issued on May 20, 2026, the question is asking what guidance NVIDIA will **reissue or update** at their Q2 earnings announcement (which appears imminent as of August 24, 2026).

Most likely scenario: NVIDIA will issue guidance for Q3 FY2027 at the Q2 earnings call. Based on the trend of ~12% sequential growth from Q1 ($81.6B) to Q2 guided mid-point (~$91B), we'd expect similar or slightly higher sequential growth for Q3 guidance.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Macro weakness or unexpected demand slowdown in data center (largest segment)
- Geopolitical constraints on China revenue tightening further
- Competition intensifying and gaining market share
- Supply chain disruptions
- Guidance conservatism after beating Q1 by ~$2B
- The $91B already issued might simply be reaffirmed with modest upward revision

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Continued strong AI/data center momentum
- Better-than-expected demand from major cloud providers (MSFT, GOOG, AMZN, META, TSLA)
- Potential relaxation of China export restrictions
- Sequential growth acceleration similar to historical patterns
- Market share gains in inference workloads
- The company exceeding Q2 guidance (as happened in Q1) leading to more bullish Q3 guidance

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides NVIDIA's actual issued guidance:
- Q2 FY2027 forward guidance: **$91.0 billion ±2%** ($89.2B - $92.8B range)
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: **$81.6 billion**
- Wall Street consensus for Q2: **~$91.9 billion**
- Sequential growth Q1→Q2: ~11.5% (from $81.6B to $91B midpoint)

Historical NVIDIA pattern from the research: Strong sequential growth continuing, with occasional beats to guidance.

---

## Reasoning for the forecast

The question is somewhat ambiguous about timing. If the Q2 earnings release has already occurred or is about to occur (Aug 24, 2026 = likely within days), then the forward guidance for Q3 FY2027 hasn't been announced yet. 

Assuming the question asks for Q3 FY2027 guidance (issued at Q2 earnings):
- Baseline: ~12% sequential growth from Q2 mid-point of $91B = ~$102B
- But companies typically guide conservatively after beats
- Accounting for modest upward revision from Q1 beat pattern: $98B-$105B likely range
- The range given (99.5B-115.5B) with open bounds suggests forecasters expected $100B-$115B as plausible

Given:
1. Strong momentum and Q1 beat pattern
2. Conservative guidance bias (±2%)
3. Likely 10-12% sequential growth continuing
4. The wide range provided

My estimate centers on **$102 billion** with reasonable uncertainty.

Median (50th percentile): 102000000000
High (90th percentile): 108000000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue, issued on May 20, 2026, is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html), [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts' average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue is around $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), which falls within NVIDIA's guided range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). In Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion in revenue, exceeding its own guidance by about $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). A similar outperformance in Q2 could push revenue near $95 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
